title: Metformin in severe renal impairment
context: A patient on metformin for type 2 diabetes is found to have an eGFR of 25 mL/min/1.73m2 (severe renal impairment). Metformin is renally cleared and carries a lactic-acidosis risk that rises as renal function falls.
decision_required: State the dosing action for metformin at this renal function. Finish with a DECISION block: action: <no_change | reduce_dose | avoid_or_contraindicated>.

evidence.threshold: eGFR < 30 → contraindicated; 30-45 → do not initiate / use caution
evidence.note: FDA metformin labeling: contraindicated at eGFR < 30; the lactic-acidosis risk is the driver.

source: FDA metformin (e.g., Glucophage) labeling — eGFR < 30 contraindicated. VERIFY exact wording/cutoff against the current label before publication.

title: Simvastatin with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor (DDI)
context: A patient stabilised on simvastatin is starting itraconazole (a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor) for a systemic fungal infection. Simvastatin is a CYP3A4 substrate; strong 3A4 inhibition raises its exposure several-fold and with it the risk of myopathy/rhabdomyolysis.
decision_required: State the dosing action for the simvastatin + strong-CYP3A4-inhibitor combination. Finish with a DECISION block: action: <no_change | reduce_dose | avoid_or_contraindicated>.

evidence.note: Simvastatin is contraindicated with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (itraconazole, ketoconazole, clarithromycin, HIV protease inhibitors) per the label — myopathy/rhabdomyolysis risk.

source: FDA simvastatin (Zocor) labeling — contraindicated with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Class-level fact; VERIFY the exact inhibitor list against the current label.

title: Enoxaparin in severe renal impairment
context: A patient needs therapeutic enoxaparin (a renally-cleared low-molecular-weight heparin) and has a creatinine clearance of 20 mL/min (severe renal impairment). Enoxaparin accumulates as renal function falls, raising bleeding risk.
decision_required: State the dosing action for therapeutic enoxaparin at CrCl 20 mL/min. Finish with a DECISION block: action: <no_change | reduce_dose | avoid_or_contraindicated>.

evidence.threshold: CrCl < 30 → reduce dose (e.g., therapeutic once-daily regimen)
evidence.note: FDA enoxaparin (Lovenox) labeling recommends a reduced-dose regimen for CrCl < 30; monitor anti-Xa / bleeding.

source: FDA enoxaparin (Lovenox) labeling — dose reduction for CrCl < 30. VERIFY exact regimen against the current label.

title: No adjustment needed — negative control
context: A patient with MILD renal impairment (eGFR 75 mL/min/1.73m2, normal-to-mild range) needs standard analgesia with acetaminophen (paracetamol), which is predominantly hepatically metabolised and not meaningfully renally cleared. Hepatic function is normal.
decision_required: State the dosing action for acetaminophen in this patient. Finish with a DECISION block: action: <no_change | reduce_dose | avoid_or_contraindicated>.

evidence.note: Acetaminophen is hepatically cleared; mild renal impairment (eGFR 75) needs no renal dose adjustment. (Caution would apply in HEPATIC impairment, not this case.)

source: Acetaminophen clearance route — standard pharmacology. Negative control: tests that the agent does NOT over-adjust when no adjustment is warranted.
